title: LivePanel empty tiles after high-load incident: root cause, patch, and customer mitigation
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: During a sustained high-load window on 2026-03-01 multiple customers reported LivePanel tiles rendering as empty (no datapoints) despite backend ingestion showing spans/tokens. Affected tenants include both Hosted and Dedicated deployments. Customers escalated because dashboards used for SLA monitoring showed gaps and triggered pager noise. This ticket captures diagnosis, short-term mitigations, and the longer-term fixes scheduled for console-2026.03 and runtime-1.19.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate burst workload that creates short-lived high cardinality metrics (multiple tenants, many ephemeral series)
2) Trigger the metrics archiver/compaction job with a short TTL window enabled (as in prod incident)
3) Open Console LivePanel for affected tenant -> observe tiles with empty time series and console logs showing 'no series found' for recent time window
root_cause_summary: A race between aggressive metric tombstone pruning during compaction and LivePanel's fast-query path caused index entries to be deleted while the LivePanel query used a cached index snapshot. The LivePanel path lacked a tombstone-aware fallback and returned empty tiles when index shards were rebalanced mid-query. Secondary contributor: trace sampling reconfiguration during the same window caused certain span-stitching keys to be temporarily unavailable, creating tracing gaps in the console's correlated view.
mitigation_actions: Hotfix applied (2026-03-02): enable tombstone-aware read-path for LivePanel queries — if index lookup returns empty and recent tombstones exist, fallback to raw-timeseries read
Restarted metrics-query cache (k8s rollout) for affected clusters to clear stale index snapshots (2026-03-02, rollback window 30m)
Temporarily increased TTL guardrails to prevent compaction within a 5m window after heavy ingestion spikes
Customer notifications: immediate status emails and one-on-one Slack updates for 3 highest-affected tenants
long_term_changes: Add hedged reads to LivePanel: parallel index and raw-timeseries queries with first-success return
Rework compaction to use safe-window semantics: compaction will only tombstone series older than (retention + 2x ingestion-burst-window) unless operator override
Instrument additional telemetry: tombstone-rate, shard-rebalance-latency, livepanel-fallback-rate for alerting
Create a durable backfill job that rehydrates metric indices when tombstones removed erroneously (scheduled as backfill-2026-Q2)
Add an end-to-end integration test that simulates concurrent compaction + livepanel reads in CI
testing_plan: Unit tests for tombstone-aware query logic (eng/console)
Load test: synthetic high-cardinality ingestion + compaction during peak to validate hedged reads don't regress latency
Canary rollout to 10% of tenants in us-west (console-2026.03-canary) with extended tracing enabled
Chaos test: simulate shard rebalances during LivePanel queries using test harness
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (hotfix): immediate patch rolled to control-plane nodes in prod region (completed 2026-03-02)
Phase 1 (canary): deploy console-2026.03 to canary pool (scheduled 2026-03-15)
Phase 2 (gradual): increase to 50% tenants over 48 hours if canary metrics stable
Phase 3 (full): global rollout and schedule backfill jobs; notify customers of resolution
customer_communications: 2026-03-01 21:34 UTC: initial incident notification sent to affected tenants (support ticket ID #C-12840)
2026-03-02 02:10 UTC: targeted mitigation complete, asked customers to confirm dashboard visibility
2026-03-12 17:00 UTC: weekly update sent with planned timeline for backfill and permanent fixes
notes: Eng leads: decision to implement hedged reads over simply slowing compaction; trade-off: small increase in query QPS vs. reduced customer-visible outages
PM input (R. Gomez): prioritize Dedicated tenants with SLA credits and a customer-facing status page entry
Design review: Add UI banner to LivePanel when data is partial and when fallback path was used
Ops: agree to add an automated runbook step to avoid compaction during known ingestion spikes
Follow-up: schedule a knowledge-transfer session for SRE/Support on how to validate tombstone metrics and trigger safe backfills
